Holds 39,767 works and had 81,147 visitors in 2024. Its Dadiani wing restoration began in 2004; the second sector opened in September 2021.
State gallery supported by the Ministry of Culture, the Senate and the EU-funded National Recovery Plan. General partner Komerční banka; others include J&T Banka, Bohemia Sekt and Czech Television.
Founders built its online school at no cost, per 24.kg (2020). Asia Art Archive is a partner on Mobile Library: Kyrgyzstan, April 2025 to June 2026.

Founded 2010. The fifth edition opened 6 December 2018. A sixth was announced for December 2020.
Ten resident-artist slots at KG 563 St, Kacyiru.
Artists' association with over 100 members. State funding ended in the civil war; a late-1990s profile names Hivos as donor.
Official foundation 1948; reopened in 1993 by young artists. Maputo's council and the CTA led a 2021 mural project with 40 of its members.
Funded by Wissam and Hiba Nesr. Wissam is chief executive of Webcor Group, a Swiss-based food importer and distributor with most African revenue in Angola.
Opened in 2021 with a residency for Angolan and Lusophone African artists; the artistic committee is chaired by Paula Nascimento.
Built on the initiative of Adama Toungara, then mayor of Abobo; the director says it was built from own funds.
Launched in 2023. The 2025 edition showed 15 artists from Congo, Sudan, Kenya and Tanzania in Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar (Musée Magazine, February 2025).

University of Pretoria gave the land and funding. The Javett Foundation funded construction and pledged ten years of annual gifts for running costs and an endowment.

Azerbaijani state project. President Ilham Aliyev ordered it built in January 2021 and opened it on 12 April 2021, according to the presidential website.

Built on a 2017 Communist Party Central Committee decision, with support from the National Development and Reform Commission, Finance Ministry and Beijing city. Entry is free.
Opened 18 June 2021. Xinhua reported more than 3.5 million visits by 30 June 2024.
Funded by China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism as a level-1 public welfare institution. The Art Newspaper counted 7.4 million visitors in 2019.
Formed 2003 by merging the Museum of the Chinese Revolution and the National Museum of Chinese History. Building opened 1959.
Founded 1985 by the Nanjing Municipal Government; the Jiangsu provincial government added a research institute in 2016. The Standard reported about 6 million visitors in 2025.

Budget unit in the Beijing government's published accounts: 809 million yuan of public funding in 2025, 711 million of it project spending.
Inside Wanping Fortress near the Marco Polo Bridge. Beijing opened a patriotic education base there for Hong Kong and Macau youth in August 2025.

Run by Cambodia's Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts, which lists it among its institutions. Foreign adults pay $5 and Cambodians enter free, the museum states.
Former Khmer Rouge prison S-21. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2025 as part of the Cambodian Memorial Sites.

Opened in 2012 in Tehran's Abbas-Abad district; about 300,000 visitors a year (AFP, 2018). The Armed Forces General Staff published its statute amendments in 2021.
Amancio Williams's house of 1943 to 1945 over the Las Chacras stream. Its restoration won the 2024 World Monuments Fund/Knoll Modernism Prize.
The architect's flat, open since October 2022. Wertinvest's Heumarkt tower put Vienna's historic centre on UNESCO's red list, 2017 to 2026.
Paul Engelmann and Ludwig Wittgenstein's house of 1928, a protected monument since 1971. It hosted a Wittgenstein exhibition in November 2024.
Thomas J. Bata recovered the villa by restitution and donated it to the foundation. Rosemarie Bata Blyth chairs the board, which includes Zlín's mayor.
Brno City Museum, funded by the City of Brno: CZK 108.3M of CZK 199.2M income in 2025. State budget and funds CZK 4.6M, South Moravian Region CZK 0.35M.

Patrons Cassina and Chanel and institutional partners DRAC Île-de-France (Ministry of Culture) and Région Île-de-France support the Fondation Le Corbusier, which runs it. Adult ticket EUR 10.
Walter Schulz's 1904 villa opposite Sopot's beach entrance 29, under renovation. The museum runs outdoor exhibitions and holds lectures at partner venues.
Reinforced-concrete house of 1916 by Rudolf Steiner and Hermann Ranzenberger, home of the Rudolf Steiner Archive since 2002. Reading room and shop open weekday afternoons.
Gaudí's 1912 apartment building, owned by the foundation created in 2012 from the savings bank CatalunyaCaixa. 909,061 visitors in 2025.

Brinkman and Van der Vlugt's 1933 museum house. The institute counted 76,035 paying visitors in 2025 across the house and its main building.
Owned by Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser, funded by rents and services (EUR 16.9M in 2025), bequests (EUR 4.3M), the VriendenLoterij (EUR 1.2M a year) and government subsidies (EUR 1.5M).
Not confirmed. The volunteer-run Mart van Schijndel Foundation (set up 2008) runs visits for a EUR 45 donation. The house is still privately lived in and no owner is named.

Old inherited money, not a large industrial fortune, per her nephew. Her mother's father owned the Newark Daily Advertiser, her father led Mutual Benefit Life.
Mackintosh's 1916 to 1917 remodelling for Bassett-Lowke. The Heritage Lottery Fund granted £999,000 towards the £1.4m 2002 to 2003 restoration.
Peter Aldington's 1967 house and garden, still the Aldington family home. He died in April 2026, and the Trust and family are planning its future.

State studio of the Korean People's Army, paid from the state budget. It makes military-themed films about the army, navy, air force and special forces (Koryo Tours).

Films pulled: Regreso a Ítaca 2014, Santa y Andrés 2016, Sueños al pairo 2020. In 2023 the Asamblea de Cineastas Cubanos denounced ICAIC censorship.
